subject: [PATCH v8 11/30] mm: split PMD swap entries into PTE swap entries

2026-10-02.patch_summary: This patch splits PMD swap entries into PTE swap entries in the Linux kernel's memory management system. The goal is to allow operations that split a PMD, such as mprotect() or munmap(), to also handle swap entries. This is achieved by adding a new branch in the __split_huge_pmd_locked() function to handle swap PMDs and convert them into PTEs. The patch also removes unnecessary reference counting for swap entries and adds tests to ensure that the correct snapshot of the old PMD is used during the conversion process.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Identified the issue with swap PMDs and acknowledged that the changes are correct. Provided a Reviewed-by tag to indicate approval of the patch.
reviews.raw_body:
On Fri Oct 2, 2026 at 5:52 AM EDT, Usama Arif wrote:
> Once a PMD can hold a swap entry, everything that splits a PMD - mprotect()
> or munmap() over part of the range, MADV_FREE, a pagewalk with no PMD
> handler - has to be able to split that entry too. A swap PMD already passes
> the pmd_is_valid_softleaf() gate, so without this it reaches
> __split_huge_pmd_locked() and falls through to the present-PMD path, which
> pmdp_invalidate()s it and calls pmd_page() on a non-present entry.
>
> No reference counting is needed: a swap entry pins no folio, and swap_map
> is already one per slot, so the PTEs simply take over what the PMD held.
>
> The migration-only entry point cannot reach the new branch:
> page_vma_mapped_walk() never hands back a swap PMD, and
> __split_huge_pmd_locked() already asserts that to_migration_entries
> implies a present or device-private PMD.
>
> Test the pre-split old_pmd rather than re-reading *pmd in the trailing
> folio_remove_rmap_pmd() gate, so every entry-type test in the function
> interrogates the same snapshot. That part is cosmetic: pmdp_invalidate()
> leaves the PMD present as far as software is concerned.
>
> Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
> ---
>  mm/huge_memory.c | 22 +++++++++++++++++++++-
>  1 file changed, 21 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
>
LGTM.

Reviewed-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

-- 
Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

2026-10-08.patch_summary: This patch series aims to split PMD swap entries into PTE swap entries, addressing a long-standing issue in the Linux kernel's memory management. The current implementation has a flaw where it fails to handle swap PMDs correctly, leading to incorrect behavior and potential crashes. This patch introduces a new branch to handle swap PMDs, ensuring that they are properly split into PTEs. The changes also include cosmetic improvements to the code, making it more efficient and easier to maintain.
